title: The Last Toast at Ravenscroft Manor
note: PLACEHOLDER story for testing the app. The real mystery replaces this in P07.
setting: A stormy evening at Ravenscroft Manor. Lady Ravenscroft has invited old friends to celebrate her 60th birthday. Halfway through her toast, she collapses.

murder_announcement.title: There has been a murder!
murder_announcement.text: As Lady Ravenscroft raised her glass for the birthday toast, she faltered, gasped, and collapsed. Dr. Thorne rushed to her side, but it was too late. Lady Cordelia Ravenscroft is dead, and the doors of the manor are locked against the storm. Someone in this room is a murderer. (PLACEHOLDER announcement.)

characters.name: Mr. Edmund Pike
characters.biography: You have served the Ravenscroft family for thirty years. You know every corridor of the manor, and every secret whispered in it.

relationships.text: You watched her grow up. Lately she has been asking odd questions about the wine cellar.
He visits Lady Ravenscroft weekly. You don't trust his smile.

secrets: TEST SECRET for PIKE: You have been quietly selling old bottles from the wine cellar for years.
objectives: Keep anyone from looking closely at the wine cellar records.
Find out who moved the birthday champagne.
characters.chapter:
PLACEHOLDER CHAPTER. The real chapter (about 10 minutes of reading) is written with the story in P07.

The rain had not stopped since noon. You moved through the east corridor of Ravenscroft Manor the way you always did, silently, counting the portraits as you passed. Thirty years in this house had taught you which floorboards complained and which doors were best left closed.

Tonight the house was full again. Voices drifted up from the drawing room, and somewhere below, the wine cellar waited in the dark, keeping your secret as faithfully as you had kept everyone else's.

knowledge.text: During the toast you stood by the dining-room door holding the tray of spare glasses, as you always do.

when_asked.says: During the toast? By the dining-room door with the spare glasses, where I always stand. I saw the whole room.

knowledge.text: You served Lady Ravenscroft for thirty years. She was demanding but fair, and you were loyal to her.

when_asked.says: Thirty years I served Her Ladyship. Demanding, yes, but fair. I was loyal to the end.

knowledge.text: Ten minutes before the toast, you saw Dr. Thorne alone by the champagne tray in the dining room, rummaging in his medical bag.

when_asked.says: I'll tell you what I saw. Dr. Thorne, alone at the champagne tray, ten minutes before the toast, with his hand in that bag of his.

knowledge.text: You have been quietly selling old bottles from the wine cellar for years.

when_asked.says: The cellar? Everything is exactly as Her Ladyship left it. I keep meticulous records.

knowledge.text: Rosalind told you this afternoon that the family solicitor visited Lady Ravenscroft this week.

when_asked.says: Family business is not mine to discuss, I'm afraid.

characters.name: Rosalind Ravenscroft
characters.biography: You are Lady Ravenscroft's only niece and, you have always assumed, her heir. You run a struggling art gallery in the city.

relationships.text: Pike has known you since childhood. He is kind, but he notices everything.
A painter your aunt has taken a sudden liking to. You find this suspicious.

secrets: TEST SECRET for ROSALIND: Your gallery is bankrupt and you owe money to dangerous people.
objectives: Find out whether your aunt changed her will.
Hide your money troubles from everyone.
characters.chapter:
PLACEHOLDER CHAPTER. The real chapter (about 10 minutes of reading) is written with the story in P07.

You arrived late on purpose. An entrance, after all, is half the battle. Your coat was soaked and your smile was perfect as you swept into the hall, already scanning the room for your aunt.

Somewhere in this house was the answer to the only question that mattered: had she changed her will? You had come to find out, and you did not intend to leave without knowing.

knowledge.text: During the toast you were standing beside your aunt, closest of anyone, smiling for the guests.

when_asked.says: I was right beside my aunt during the toast. Closer than anyone. I saw her fall.

knowledge.text: You resented your aunt's control over your life and money, but you also loved her.

when_asked.says: She was my aunt. Family is... complicated. That's all.

knowledge.text: You never touched the champagne tray; Pike served everyone's glass.

when_asked.says: I didn't touch the champagne. Pike served everyone. Ask him.

knowledge.text: At lunch, your aunt told you she was 'making some changes' to her will.

when_asked.says: My aunt and I never discussed money. Never.

knowledge.text: Before dinner you saw Juniper slip a sealed letter into your aunt's handbag.

when_asked.says: I saw that painter, Juniper, slip a sealed letter into my aunt's handbag before dinner. Ask her about that.

knowledge.text: Your gallery is bankrupt and you owe money to dangerous people.

when_asked.says: The art world has its ups and downs, darling. Next question.

characters.name: Dr. Silas Thorne
characters.biography: You have been Lady Ravenscroft's doctor for a decade. You are charming, careful, and always carry your medical bag.

relationships.text: The butler watches you too closely. You suspect he dislikes you.
Rosalind once asked you, oddly, how long her aunt might live.

secrets: TEST SECRET for THORNE: You lost your medical licence in another country under a different name.
objectives: Find out who opened your medical bag during dinner.
characters.chapter:
PLACEHOLDER CHAPTER. The real chapter (about 10 minutes of reading) is written with the story in P07.

Your medical bag sat by your feet at dinner, as it always did. The guests found it reassuring. A doctor at the table, just in case.

You smiled, passed the salt, and listened. A careful man listens more than he speaks, and you had been careful for a very long time.

knowledge.text: During the toast you stood next to Lady Ravenscroft, close enough to swap her glass. You claim you were by the fireplace.

when_asked.says: Where was I? By the fireplace, warming my hands, nowhere near her.

knowledge.text: Lady Ravenscroft was your patient for ten years and paid you generously.

when_asked.says: She was my patient for ten years. A generous woman. This is a great loss.

knowledge.text: You added powder from a glass vial in your medical bag to Lady Ravenscroft's champagne just before the toast.

when_asked.says: I never went near the champagne. I was by the fireplace the whole time.
when_asked.confession: That vial... all right. Yes. I put it in her glass. She knew who I really was, and she was going to ruin me.

knowledge.text: Last week Lady Ravenscroft confronted you about the name you used to practise under abroad.

when_asked.says: We had a perfectly cordial relationship. She was my patient and my friend.

knowledge.text: You noticed Pike watching you closely all evening.

when_asked.says: That butler hasn't taken his eyes off me all night. Ask him why.

characters.name: Juniper Vale
characters.biography: You are a young painter whom Lady Ravenscroft recently 'discovered'. She commissioned her birthday portrait from you.

relationships.text: Rosalind runs a gallery and has been cold to you all evening.
The doctor looked startled when he first saw you, as if he recognised you.

secrets: TEST SECRET for JUNIPER: You are Lady Ravenscroft's secret granddaughter, and she told you so last week.
objectives: Decide whether to reveal who you really are.
Learn why the doctor seemed to recognise you.
characters.chapter:
PLACEHOLDER CHAPTER. The real chapter (about 10 minutes of reading) is written with the story in P07.

The portrait was finished, wrapped in brown paper, leaning against the wall of the guest room you had been given. You had painted her eyes three times before they looked right.

She had told you a secret last week, one that changed everything you thought you knew about yourself. Tonight, among all these strangers who were not quite strangers, you would have to decide what to do with it.

knowledge.text: During the toast you stood at the back of the room beside your covered portrait.

when_asked.says: I was at the back, next to my portrait. I was waiting to unveil it after the toast.

knowledge.text: Lady Ravenscroft commissioned your portrait and treated you with unusual warmth.

when_asked.says: She commissioned my portrait. She was... unusually kind to me.

knowledge.text: You were handed a glass by Pike but didn't drink; you were too nervous about the unveiling.

when_asked.says: Pike handed me a glass, but I didn't drink it. I was too nervous about the unveiling.

knowledge.text: Last week Lady Ravenscroft told you that you are her granddaughter.

when_asked.says: She was very kind to me. That's all I'll say for now.

knowledge.text: Right after the toast you saw Dr. Thorne wipe his hands on a napkin, looking pale.

when_asked.says: Right after the toast, the doctor was wiping his hands on a napkin. He looked white as a sheet.

knowledge.text: In the hallway you overheard Pike muttering about 'missing bottles'.

when_asked.says: I heard Pike in the hallway muttering about 'missing bottles'. I don't know what he meant.

solution.motive: Lady Ravenscroft discovered Dr. Thorne's false identity and planned to expose him after the party.
solution.method: He added poison from his medical bag to her champagne glass while everyone gathered for the toast.

casting_note: casting.load is 'major' or 'low-pressure'. casting.needs: the minimum answer (1-4) a guest should give on that question. casting.content: sensitive content ('killer', 'romance') that guests can refuse.

directions.text: PLACEHOLDER: Excuse yourself and 'check the wine cellar'. Come back looking flustered, but don't explain why.
PLACEHOLDER: Ask Pike, loudly enough to be overheard, whether your aunt's solicitor visited this week.
PLACEHOLDER: Offer to 'examine' the champagne glass. Keep everyone else away from it.
PLACEHOLDER: Unveil the birthday portrait to the room and say something kind about Lady Ravenscroft.

'text' is the private truth (used for REMEMBER). when_asked.stance (truth/evade/lie) and when_asked.says decide what they say when INTERROGATED; the AI only ever sees 'says' for lies and evasions. confess_with lists evidence ids that unlock the confession.

views.painter: Your heart races. 'J'... this must be for you.

views.butler: Your own corrections. Anyone who looks closely will see they don't match.

missions.text: Refill three guests' glasses and casually ask each where they were during the toast.
Find out who 'J' is without ever saying the letter J out loud.
Convince two guests that Pike had more access to the champagne than anyone.
Make a toast to Lady Ravenscroft that mentions her portrait.

clues_note: clues: things guests find. With a 'code' it has a printable QR label for a prop (prop/where are for the host only). 'text' is what everyone sees; 'views' adds what a specific character notices. 'evidence' is added to the finder's evidence (for confessions). Essential clues need a 'backup' route. Clues without a code are bonus clues, given by missions or by the host. missions: secret tasks the host confirms; each rewards one clue.
